name: Joep Langebrug
en: Joep Langebrug (bridge 417) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid.

name: Joes Kloppenburgbrug
en: The Joes Kloppenburgbrug, bridge no. 5, is a slab bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Raamsteeg with the Oude Spiegelstraat and crosses the Singel. It is a relatively narrow and slightly humped bridge with three openings for shipping, decorated with a granite artwork.

name: Johan Cruijffbrug
en: The Johan Cruijffbrug (bridge 2238) is a structural work of art in the Dutch district of Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is a pedestrian and bicycle bridge; it forms the connection between the Esplanade de Meer square and the Anfieldroad (street) towards Middenweg. It lies parallel to the Johan Neeskensbrug over a decorative water.

name: Johan Cruijffbrug
en: The Johan Cruijffbrug (bridge 2238) is a structure in the Amsterdam-Oost borough. It is a foot and cycle bridge connecting the Esplanade de Meer square with the Anfieldroad towards the Middenweg. It runs parallel to the Johan Neeskensbrug over an ornamental water in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer.

name: Johan Neeskensbrug
en: The Johan Neeskensbrug (bridge 2237) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the few traffic bridges here — most are for slow traffic only — and lies in the Wembleylaan over an ornamental water in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer, built between 1998 and 2002 and entirely surrounded by a ring ditch.

name: Johan Neeskensbrug
en: The Johan Neeskensbrug (bridge 2237) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is one of the few traffic bridges (most are only for slow traffic); it is located on Wembleylaan over a decorative water in the area near Park de Meer, Watergraafsmeer that rose from the ground here between 1998 and 2002.

name: Johanna Borskibrug
en: The Johanna Borskibrug (bridge number 41) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the Vijzelstraat and spans the Keizersgracht.

name: John Rädeckerbrug
en: The John Rädeckerbrug (bridge 1916) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. It lies in the Th. K. van Lohuizenlaan, called IJburglaan until 1998, and crosses the Lozingskanaal. Together with the similar Ad Grimmonbrug (bridge 1915) it connects the Zeeburg district with Cruquiuseiland; the two bridges share a history and an appearance.

name: John Rädeckerbrug
en: The John Rädeckerbrug (bridge 1916) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. It is located in the Th. K. van Lohuizenlaan, formerly called Ijburglaan until 1998 and crosses the Lozingskanaal. Together with the similar Ad Grimmonbrug (bridge 1915), it forms the connection between the Zeeburg district and the Cruquiuseiland.

name: Johnny & Jonesbrug
en: The Johnny & Jonesbrug (bridge 433) is a fixed bridge in the Prinses Irenebuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. The footbridge crosses the entrance to the circular central pond of the Beatrixpark, beside the perennial garden. Jan Trapman's sculpture Pinguïns stands nearby. The park dates from 1936-1938.

name: Johnny & Jonesbrug
en: The Johnny & Jonesbrug (bridge 433) is a fixed bridge in the Prinses Irenebuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. The pedestrian bridge is located over the entrance to the circular central large pond of Beatrixpark. It is located next to the "permanent botanical garden". In the immediate vicinity stands the sculpture Penguins by Jan Trapman.

name: Kabouterbrug
en: The Kabouterbrug (Bridge 360) is a steel lift bridge in Amsterdam-Zuid that is only accessible to pedestrians and cyclists. The bridge is located on a continuous cycling route from Vondelpark via Schinkelhavenstraat towards Amsterdam Nieuw-West to Theophile de Bockstraat. It spans the Schinkel, which is part of the Staandemast route here, and connects d

name: Kabouterbrug
en: The Kabouterbrug (bridge 360) is a steel drawbridge in Amsterdam-Zuid, open only to pedestrians and cyclists. It lies on a through cycle route from the Vondelpark via the Schinkelhavenstraat towards Amsterdam Nieuw-West and the Theophile de Bockstraat. It spans the Schinkel, part of the Staandemastroute here.

name: Kadoelenbrug
en: The Kadoelenbrug (bridge 1787) is a bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. The name refers to the Kadoelen area north of the bridge. It was built between 29 August 2011 and May 2013 for just under 2.5 million euros, although the official opening took place on 4 July 2012.

name: Kattenburgerbrug
en: The Kattenburgerbrug (bridge 274) is a bascule bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The wide traffic bridge forms the connection between on one side the Prins Hendrikkade and the Kadijksplein (both southwest) and on the other side the Kattenburgerstraat, Kattenburgerplein and the Kattenburgergracht (northeast).

name: Kattenburgerbrug
en: The Kattenburgerbrug (bridge 274) is a bascule bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The wide traffic bridge connects the Prins Hendrikkade and the Kadijksplein to the south-west with the Kattenburgerstraat, Kattenburgerplein and Kattenburgergracht to the north-east. The boundary between the Oosterdok and the Nieuwe Vaart runs beneath it.

name: Kattenrugbrug
en: De Katterug (bridge no. 1935) is a bridge over the Hugo de Grootgracht in Amsterdam-West. It connects the foot and cycle path continuing from the Van Reigersbergenstraat and the Hugo de Grootkade with the Bilderdijkpark, and lies in line with the Bilderdijkkade. It owes its name to its rather steep slope and profile, recalling a cat's back.

name: Kattenrugbrug
en: The Katterug (bridge no. 1935) is a bridge over the Hugo de Grootgracht in Amsterdam-West. en: The Kees Fensbrug (bridge number 49) is a permanent viaduct bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge forms the connection between the Hartenstraat and Reestraat and spans the Keizersgracht. There has already been a bridge here for at least a century since the municipality of Amsterdam decided in 1881 that the bridge should be lowered.

name: Kees Fensbrug
en: The Kees Fensbrug (bridge number 49) is a fixed arched bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Hartenstraat with the Reestraat, spanning the Keizersgracht. A bridge had stood here for at least a century when the city decided in 1881 that it had to be lowered.

name: Keizersbrug
en: The Keizersbrug (bridge 286) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in line with the Korte Koningsstraat and crosses the Oudeschans. Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode's city map of 1625 and Joan Blaeu's of 1649 both show two bridges over the Oudeschans, then still called the Montelbaens Burchwal.

name: Keizersgrachtkerk
en: The Keizersgrachtkerk is a church of 1888, originally Reformed, on the Amsterdam Keizersgracht. The building at number 566, between the Leidsestraat and the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat, was designed by the architects Gerlof Bartholomeus Salm and Abraham Salm, father and son.

name: Kerk van Zunderdorp
en: The Kerk van Zunderdorp is the Reformed Dutch Kerk van Zunderdorp in Amsterdam-North. It is a plastered hall church with buttresses, built in 1711 against the late Gothic tower without buttresses of the previous church. The tower dates back to the 15th century, has three floors and is equipped with a balustrade and a tent roof.

name: Kerk van Zunderdorp
en: The Kerk van Zunderdorp is the Dutch Reformed church of Zunderdorp in Amsterdam-Noord. It is a plastered hall church with buttresses, built in 1711 against the late Gothic tower of the previous church, which has none. The 15th-century tower has three stages, a balustrade and a tent roof.

name: Ketelhuis
en: Het Ketelhuis is a Dutch film theater that has been located in the Westergasfabriek cultural park in Amsterdam since 1999. Dutch films, European arthouse films, documentaries and family films are screened.

name: Kinkerbrug
en: The Kinkerbrug (bridge no. 266) is a bridge over the Kostverlorenvaart in Amsterdam-West. It connects the Kinkerstraat with the Postjesweg and the Witte de Withstraat, and between 1990 and 2010 formed the boundary between the former boroughs of De Baarsjes and Oud-West.

It crosses the Nieuwe Leeuwarderweg, which is surrounded here by the Noorderpark and formerly cut through the Volewijkspark. It dates from 2010/2011 and consists of a long, slightly arched concrete span on two concrete trestle piers.

en: The Korte Ouderkerkerbrug (bridge 1962) is a cycle and foot bridge in the Overamstel district on the right bank of the Amstel in Amsterdam-Oost. It spans the Duivendrechtsevaart, connecting the western part of the Korte Ouderkerkerdijk, just past the Zuidergasfabriekbrug (bridge 311) where the cycle path begins, with the Joan Muyskenweg.

name: Korte Ouderkerkerbrug
en: The Korte Ouderkerkerbrug (bridge 1962) is a bicycle and pedestrian bridge located in the Overamstel district on the right Amstel Riverbank in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Kraan 2868
en: Kraan 2868, also called the Figeekraan, is a former harbour crane on KNSM-eiland in Amsterdam-Oost. It is a luffing crane, with a jib adjustable in height rather than fixed, and has been a municipal monument since 29 November 2011.

name: Krijtbergbrug
en: The Krijtbergsluis (bridge no. 3) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the southwestern quay of the Singel and spans the Beulingsloot in the Amsterdam canal belt.

name: Krijtbergbrug
en: The Krijtbergsluis (bridge no. 3) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the south-western quay of the Singel and spans the Beulingsloot in Amsterdam's canal ring. A bridge has been here for centuries: Joan Blaeu's map of around 1649 already shows it, along with the buildings standing directly on the water at the Beulingsloot.

name: Kriterion
en: Film theater Kriterion, officially the Association for Mutual Student Support Kriterion (V.O.S.S. Kriterion), is a student-run cinema and student association at Roetersstraat 170 in Amsterdam. It emerged from the student resistance during World War II.

name: Kunstenaarsverzet
en: The Monument voor het kunstenaarsverzet 1940-1945 is an artistic work and memorial in Amsterdam-Centrum. The demolition of the Panoramagebouw at Plantage Middenlaan 50 left a relatively broad strip of green, which was named the Plantage Westermanlaan in 1963 and became a public garden without officially being called one.

name: L.H. Sarlouisbrug
en: The L.H. Sarlouisbrug (bridge 240) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge lies in the Weesperstraat and spans the Nieuwe Keizersgracht. Its history resembles that of the Dr. Dünnerbrug and the Dr. Meijer de Hondbrug, though it is somewhat older, given how the city developed outwards from the centre.

en: The Lau Mazirelbrug (bridge 259) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge was named in 1982 after lawyer and resistance fighter Lau Mazirel (1907-1974). The traffic bridge forms the connection between the quay of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht, the Nieuwe Kerkstraat and Roetersstraat from the southwest and the Plantage Kerklaan from the northeast.

name: Lau Mazirelbrug
en: The Lau Mazirelbrug (bridge 259) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum, named in 1982 after the lawyer and resistance fighter Lau Mazirel (1907-1974). The traffic bridge connects the quay of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht, the Nieuwe Kerkstraat and the Roetersstraat from the south-west with the Plantage Kerklaan from the north-east.

name: Laurenskerk
en: The Grote or Laurenskerk is a church building on Kerkstraat/Nieuwstraat in the center of the North Holland town of Weesp. The church was built between 1429 and 1462 as a late Gothic cruciform church, on the site where a Romanesque church had previously stood. From 1489, a seven-hour college was attached to the church with paid and professional singers.

name: Laurenskerk
en: The Grote or Laurenskerk is a church on the Kerkstraat and Nieuwstraat in the centre of Weesp, North Holland. It was built between 1429 and 1462 as a late Gothic cruciform church on the site of an earlier Romanesque church. From 1489 a college of seven canonical hours with paid professional singers was attached to it.

name: Lee Millerbrug
en: The Lee Millerbrug (bridge 2080) is a bridge still to be built in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge will be built in 2023 and 2024 and will provide the connection between Centrumeiland and Strandeiland within the IJburg district in Pampuslaan. The bridge will then span the Merdekagracht.

name: Lee Millerbrug

It is being built in 2023 and 2024 and will carry the Pampuslaan between Centrumeiland and Strandeiland within the IJburg district, spanning the Merdekagracht. It was named on 6 July 2021 after the photographer and war correspondent Lee Miller.

The first plans for a bridge here date from 1916, when the site was leased to the Dordtsche Petroleum Maatschappij.

It connects the Leidseplein and the Marnixstraat with the Leidsebosje and the Stadhouderkade, and is named after the former Leidsepoort. Its abutments and piers were made of natural stone.

name: Lekstraatsynagoge
en: The Lekstraat Synagogue stands at Lekstraat 63 in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam. It is an important centre for the Haredi Jews living in Amsterdam and the surrounding area. Several hundred Haredim live in Amstelveen and Amsterdam, mainly in the Rivierenbuurt and Buitenveldert.

Just before the bridge the water is pumped up out of a pond and then flows through an artificial channel and fall into the large pond.

A bridge has been here for centuries: it is drawn on Pieter Bast's map of 1599, running from the Lijnbaan Steech to the Blaeuwe Burchwal.

name: Lijnderbrug
en: The Lijnderbrug is a lift bridge between the Amsterdamse Baan (T106) in Lijnden (Haarlemmermeer municipality) in the province of North Holland and the Ookmeerweg (s106) in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The bridge spans, at more than 4 meters high, the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder and the Akerdijk, 500 meters southeast of the De Lynden Pump Station.

name: Lijnderbrug
en: The Lijnderbrug is a drawbridge between the Amsterdamse Baan (T106) in Lijnden, in the municipality of Haarlemmermeer, and the Ookmeerweg (s106) in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. At more than 4 metres above the water it spans the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder and the Akerdijk, 500 metres south-east of the De Lynden pumping station.

name: Living by Numbers
en: The HIV/AIDS monument is an artistic work on De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam-Centrum, unveiled on 1 December 2016. The work by Jean-Michel Othoniel stands on De Ruijterkade. The initiative came around 2013 from the Stichting Namen Project Nederland, which asked a number of artists for a monument.

name: Living by Numbers

The creation of Jean-Michel Othoniel is located on De Ruijterkade, Amsterdam. name: LJG
en: The Liberal Jewish Congregation of Amsterdam (LJG) is the local community of liberal Jews in Amsterdam and its surroundings, with a synagogue in Amsterdam-Zuid since 1957. Since 2010 the LJG has had a new synagogue and cultural centre on the Zuidelijke Wandelweg, near the Gaasterlandstraat.

name: LJG
en: The Liberal Jewish Community of Amsterdam (LJG) is the local community of the liberal Jews in the Dutch city of Amsterdam and its surroundings, with (since 1957) a synagogue in Amsterdam-Zuid. Since 2010, the LJG has had a new synagogue with cultural center on the Zuidelijke Wandelweg, near the Gaasterlandstraat.

name: Lodewijk van Deysselstraat

name: Luther Museum Amsterdam
en: The Luther Museum Amsterdam, formerly known as the Luther Collection Amsterdam, is a museum that wants to introduce the public to Lutheranism in the Netherlands and Amsterdam, the role of Wittenberg as a center of administration and the works of the diaconate in the past and present, with a collection of art and historical objects related to Lutheranism.

name: M. Justbrug

name: M. Justbrug

The roughly 35-metre-wide traffic bridge dates from 1961 and is a culvert bridge, carried over a four-metre concrete box culvert.

name: Maarten Lutherkerk
en: The Maarten Luther Kerk is a church building in the Rivierenbuurt in Amsterdam-Zuid. It was designed for the Evangelical Lutheran church in the Amsterdam School style by the architect F. Jantzen.

name: Machineslootbrug

name: Madibabrug
en: The Madibabrug (bridge 1035) is a structure in Amsterdam-Zuidoost. It lies in the Karspeldreef and crosses the Reigersbospad. The Karspeldreef, on an embankment, cuts through the Nelson Mandelapark from east to west and is open only to fast traffic, while the Reigersbospad for pedestrians and cyclists crosses the park from north to south.

name: Madibabrug

name: Mahatma Gandhi
en: Mahatma Gandhi is an artwork in Amsterdam-Zuid, depicting Mahatma Gandhi walking with a stick in his hand. It came about thanks to the Stichting Standbeeld Mahatma Gandhi, mainly made up of Indian and Surinamese supporters of Gandhi's ideas, who had been working since around 1972 to have a statue of him erected.

name: Max Euwe Centrum
en: The Max Euwe Centrum is a chess centre on the Max Euweplein in Amsterdam. It consists of a small museum about the chess career and life of the Dutch world champion Max Euwe (1901-1981) and a meeting centre and library with around eleven thousand books and periodicals.

name: Meerpadkerk
en: The Meerpadkerkje is a small white-painted wooden Mennonite meeting house in Nieuwendam, now part of Amsterdam-Noord, built in 1843 by the Nieuwendam carpenter Pieter Kater Gzn. The church belongs to the United Mennonite Congregation of Amsterdam and has been protected as a national monument since 1970.

name: Meervaart Theater
en: Meervaart is a theater and a convention center in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. Meervaart is a contemporary metropolitan theater where audiences and creators with diverse backgrounds, taste preferences and ambitions come into contact with each other. Meervaart connects the neighborhood, the city and the wider world with each other.

Buildings, streets and bridges here are named after things to do with football: the district was built where Stadion De Meer, for years the home of AFC Ajax, stood until 1996.

name: Mien Ruysbrug
en: The Mien Ruysbrug (bridge 1944) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge was built in connection with the renovation of Park Frankendael. It had accumulated a backlog of maintenance over the years and was prepared for the modern era under the leadership of architectural firm Sant and Co by Edwin Santhagens. name: Mien Ruysbrug
en: The Mien Ruysbrug (bridge 1944) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It was built as part of the renovation of Park Frankendael, which had fallen behind on maintenance over the years and was brought up to date under the architects Sant en Co of Edwin Santhagens, with the path system reworked.

name: Molen van Sloten
en: The Molen van Sloten is a polder mill in the village of Sloten near Amsterdam. It is an octagonal oak smock mill with a thatched roof on a stone base. It stands on the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder and, together with the Aker pumping station, drains the Westelijke Tuinsteden.

name: Molen van Sloten
en: The Molen van Sloten is a polder mill in the village of Sloten near Amsterdam. It is an oak-wooden, thatched octagonal tower mill on a stone base. The mill is located on the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeerpolder and together with the Akergemaal provides the irrigation of the Western Garden Cities. name: Monument Haarlemmerweg
en: The Monument aan de Haarlemmerweg commemorates war victims and stands on the Haarlemmerweg in Amsterdam Nieuw-West, between the Burgemeester Eliasstraat and Burgemeester Fockstraat foot and cycle bridges. Police officer Elias and Verkuijl, father and son, were shot here by the German occupiers in reprisal for an act of resistance on the railway.

name: Monument Haarlemmerweg
en: The Monument on the Haarlemmerweg is a monument for war victims, placed on the Haarlemmerweg, Amsterdam Nieuw-West between the pedestrian and bicycle bridges Burgemeester Eliasstraat and Burgemeester Fockstraat. Police officer Elias' father and son Verkuijl were shot dead here by the German occupiers as revenge for a resistance act on the railway track

name: Monument van voetbalclub BPC
en: The municipality of Amsterdam has 197 war memorials.

name: Monument voor gefusilleerde verzetstrijders
en: The Verzetsmonument Apollolaan is an artwork in Amsterdam-Zuid. The monument, to a design by Jan Havermans, stands in the central reservation of the Apollolaan west of its crossing with the Beethovenstraat. On 24 October 1944 the German occupiers brought 29 prisoners from the Weteringschans house of detention to this spot.

name: Monument voor gefusilleerde verzetstrijders
en: The Resistance Monument Apollolaan is a work of art in Amsterdam-Zuid. The monument, designed by Jan Havermans, was placed in the center median of the Apollolaan west of its intersection with Beethovenstraat. On that spot, on October 24, 1944, 29 prisoners from the Weteringschans Detention Center were brought to this place by the German occupiers.

name: Monument Walraven van Hall
en: The Monument Walraven van Hall is a work of art and war monument in Amsterdam-Centrum. name: Monument Walraven van Hall
en: The Monument Walraven van Hall is an artwork and war memorial in Amsterdam-Centrum. The sculpture was initiated by the retired general practitioner Hans Weijers and the retired physician Loek van Buchem, who set up a foundation to raise a monument to the resistance member Walraven van Hall.

name: Mor Sharbil
en: The building at Burgemeester Eliasstraat 72-74 in Amsterdam-Slotermeer has been a municipal monument since 2011. A new Sint-Catharinakerk went up on this spot in 1954, after the old church was demolished in 1939. It was built to a design by the architects Evers en Sarlemijn, who put the work out to tender in July 1954.

name: Mor Sharbil
en: The building Burgemeester Eliasstraat 72-74 in Amsterdam-Slotermeer Amsterdam has been a municipal monument since 2011. In 1954, a new Sint-Catharinakerk was built on this site, after the old church was demolished in 1939. The church was completed in a design by the architectural firm Evers and Sarlemijn, which carried out the tender in July 1954.

name: Moskee El-Hijra
en: The Olive Branch was built in 1956 as a Baptist church on Arthur van Schendelstraat in the garden city of Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The building from the reconstruction period is characteristic of the work of architect Karel Sijmons.

name: Moskee El-Hijra
en: De Olijftak was built in 1956 as a Mennonite church on the Arthur van Schendelstraat in the garden city of Slotermeer in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The post-war building is characteristic of the work of the architect Karel Sijmons. It went out of use as a Mennonite church in 1969 and was then sold to the Reformed Church.

name: Muiderbergbrug
en: The Muiderbergbrug (bridge 989) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. The foot and cycle bridge lies in line with the Markengouw in Nieuwendam. It dates from 1968/1969 and is built of concrete — span, piers and abutments — with steel balustrades painted blue, a colour found on several structures in this neighbourhood.

name: Muiderbergbrug
en: The Muiderbergbrug (bridge 989) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-North. The foot and bicycle bridge is along the Markengouw in Nieuwendam. The bridge dates back to 1968/1969 and consists of concrete (a concrete span, concrete pillars, concrete abutments) with blue painted steel balustrades. This color is more common in this area. name: Muiderkerk
en: The Muiderkerk is a Protestant church on Linnaeusstraat in Amsterdam-Oost, on the edge of Oosterpark. The old Muiderkerk, built in 1892, partially burned down in 1989 but the distinctive tower remained unscathed. The current Muiderkerk is built against the old tower and is part of a 1997 construction complex designed by architect Van Hoogeve

name: Muiderpoort
en: The Muiderpoort in Amsterdam is a city gate on the Alexanderplein, at the crossing of the Plantage Middenlaan with the Sarphatistraat. The gate was part of Amsterdam's fortifications. On either side lie bridge 264, over the Plantage Muidergracht by Artis, and bridge 265, over the Singelgracht to the Tropenmuseum on the Mauritskade.

name: Muiderpoort
en: The Muiderpoort in Amsterdam is a city gate on Alexanderplein, at the intersection of Plantage Middenlaan and Sarphatistraat. The gate was part of the fortifications of Amsterdam. On either side of the gate are bridge 264 (over the Plantage Muidergracht near Artis) and bridge 265 (over the Singelgracht to Het Tropenmuseum on the Mauritskade).

name: Muiderspoorbrug
en: The Muiderspoorbrug bridge between Diemen and Weesp spans the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal and is part of the Amsterdam-Zutphen railway line and since 1993 also of the Weesp-Leiden railway line. The first railway bridge at this location was built in 1892 when the Merwedekanaal was constructed. This later merged into the Amsterdam-Rhine Canal.

name: Muiderspoorbrug
en: The Muiderspoorbrug between Diemen and Weesp crosses the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal and forms part of the Amsterdam-Zutphen railway and, since 1993, of the Weesp-Leiden railway as well. The first railway bridge here was built in 1892 when the Merwedekanaal was dug; that canal was later absorbed into the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal.

name: Muntsluis
en: The Muntsluis (bridge no. 1) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. Although it carries number 1, it is not the first bridge of Amsterdam. The word sluis is used here in the sense of a stone bridge, not a water barrier. It crosses the point where the Singel flows into the Amstel, connecting the east quay of the Singel with the far side.

name: Muntsluis
en: The Muntsluis (bridge no. 1) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. Although the bridge bears the name number 1, it is not the first bridge of Amsterdam. The name sluice is used here in the meaning of "stone bridge", not as a water dam. The bridge is located over the place where the Singel flows into the Amstel.

name: Museum Amsterdam Noord
en: Museum Amsterdam Noord is a Dutch cultural history museum on the corner of Zamenhofstraat and Meeuwenlaan in Amsterdam-North. name: Museum Amsterdam Noord
en: Museum Amsterdam Noord is a cultural history museum on the corner of the Zamenhofstraat and the Meeuwenlaan in Amsterdam-Noord. Since April 2009 it has occupied the bathhouse built in 1919 for Vogeldorp; the houses in that garden village had no bathrooms, so a bathhouse was necessary.

name: Museum De Dageraad
en: De Dageraad is a housing complex in Amsterdam-Zuid. It lies on both sides of the P.L. Takstraat and is among the aesthetic high points of the Amsterdam School. In 1920 the socialist housing association De Dageraad commissioned the architects Michel de Klerk and Piet Kramer to build 294 homes and six shops.

name: Museum De Dageraad
en: De Dageraad is a residential complex in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is located on either side of the P.L. Takstraat and is one of the aesthetic highlights of the Amsterdam School. name: Museum of the Canals
en: Grachtenmuseum Amsterdam, the Museum of the Canals, is a museum on the Herengracht in Amsterdam devoted to the 17th-century Amsterdam canal ring and the history of the city. It occupies a seventeenth-century canal house with classical period rooms, a permanent multimedia exhibition, a canal garden and temporary exhibitions.

name: Museum of the Canals
en: Grachtenmuseum Amsterdam (Museum of the Canals) is a museum on the Herengracht in Amsterdam dedicated to the 17th-century Amsterdam canal belt and the history of Amsterdam. name: Museum Weesp
en: Museum Weesp is located on the second floor of the Weesp Town Hall in the Dutch province of North Holland. It highlights the history of Weesp, whose history is related to porcelain, cocoa and bicycles. The museum began in 1911 as an antiquities room within the town hall. name: Museum Weesp
en: Museum Weesp is on the second floor of the town hall of Weesp in the province of North Holland. It covers the history of Weesp, which is bound up with porcelain, cocoa and bicycles. The museum began in 1911 as an antiquities room within the town hall, and became a museum in 1974 after a gift of porcelain.

name: Muurschildering Johan Cruijff
en: The Johan Cruijff mural is a wall painting in Amsterdam-Watergraafsmeer. The portrait of Johan Cruijff was painted in 2017 on the side wall of a block of flats on the Anfieldroad, at right angles to the Wembleylaan. Those streets were laid out on the grounds of the former AFC Ajax ground Stadion De Meer.

name: Muurschildering Johan Cruijff
en: The Muurschildering Johan Cruijff is a mural in Amsterdam-Watergraafsmeer. The portrait of Johan Cruyff was installed in 2017 on the side facade of a residential apartment building, which is located on Anfieldroad, perpendicular to Wembleylaan. Those streets were laid out on the grounds of the former AFC Ajax stadium Stadion De Meer.

name: NACO-house
en: The office of Koppe's Scheepsagentuur, also known as the NACO-huisje, is a former shipping office on De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designated a national monument in 2002 for its combination of the Amsterdam School with a foreign building style, particularly in the roof. Since 13 December 2021 it has stood by bridge 2274 over the Oostertoegang.

name: NACO-house
en: The Office of Koppe's Shipping Agency, also known as the NACO cottage, is a former shipping office on the De Ruijterkade in Amsterdam-Centrum. It was designated as a national monument in 2002 due to the combination of Amsterdam School and an exotic architectural style, especially in the chapel.

name: Nassaukerk
en: The Nassaukerk is a Protestant church of 1926 on the De Wittenkade in the Staatsliedenbuurt in Amsterdam-West.

name: Nationaal monument Slavernijverleden
en: The Nationaal Monument Slavernijverleden is a monument in the Oosterpark in Amsterdam to commemorate the abolition of slavery in the Dutch Kingdom. The statue is made of bronze and the base is made of concrete.

name: Nicolaas Beetsstraat
en: The Hennetjesbrug (bridge 179) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West. It lies in the Nicolaas Beetsstraat and spans the Jacob van Lennepkanaal. The former grounds of the Wilhelmina Gasthuis lay to its south-east. A drawbridge for traffic opened here in May 1889, designed by Bastiaan de Greef, the city architect.

name: Nieuwe Amstelbrug
en: The Nieuwe Amstelbrug (bridge no. 101) in Amsterdam is a double bascule bridge over the Amstel on the border between De Pijp in Amsterdam-South and Amsterdam-East. The bridge forms the river crossing between the Ceintuurbaan and Amsteldijk (formerly Utrechtsezijde) on the one hand and Weesperzijde, Ruyschstraat and Eerste Oosterparkstraat on the other.

name: Nieuwe Amstelbrug
en: The Nieuwe Amstelbrug (bridge no. 101) in Amsterdam is a double bascule bridge over the Amstel on the boundary between De Pijp in Amsterdam-Zuid and Amsterdam-Oost. It links the Ceintuurbaan and Amsteldijk, formerly Utrechtsezijde, with the Weesperzijde, Ruyschstraat and Eerste Oosterparkstraat.

name: Nieuwe-Wercksbrug
en: The Nieuwe-Wercksbrug (bridge no. 63) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Westermarkt with the Rozengracht, spanning the Prinsengracht at the Oude Wester.

name: Nieuwendammerkerk
en: The Nieuwendammerkerk is the village church of the dyke village of Nieuwendam in Amsterdam-Noord. It does not stand along the Nieuwendammerdijk but slightly lower behind it on the Brede Kerkepad. It is a handsomely sited village church with a graveyard around it.

name: Nollewoudsbrug
en: Brug 432 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Noord. The traffic bridge, long carrying bus line 32 and since 2018 line 35, lies in the Purmerweg and Nieuwe Purmerweg and spans the ring ditch of the Buikslotermeer. There have been three versions: it began in 1937 as a wooden bridge in open countryside, with no buildings yet around it.

name: Nollewoudsbrug
en: Bridge 432 is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-North. The traffic bridge, over which bus line 32 used to run, since 2018 bus line 35, is located in the Purmerweg / Nieuwe Purmerweg and spans the ring ditch of the Buikslotermeer. There are three versions of this bridge. It began in 1937 as a wooden bridge in a rural area; there is no buildings yet to be found.

name: NSM-brug
en: The NSM-brug (bridge 356) is a bascule bridge in the Klaprozenweg, spanning Zijkanaal I in Amsterdam-Noord. The bridge opened on 22 April 2018 is the third version. It mattered for opening up Tuindorp Oostzaan and was originally a single steel drawbridge connected to its abutments by many approach spans.

name: NSM-brug
en: The NSM-brug (bridge 356) is a bascule bridge located in the Klaprozenweg and spans the Zijkanaal I in Amsterdam-Noord. The bridge that was opened on April 22, 2018 is the third version. name: Odebrug
en: The Odebrug, or ODE-brug, short for Oosterdokseiland, is a fixed bridge in the centre of Amsterdam connecting Oosterdokseiland with the Prins Hendrikkade. It is made of prefabricated concrete elements, steel and aluminium and consists of three parts. The pedestrian deck is finished with finely ground basalt grit.

name: Odebrug
en: The Odebrug or ODE bridge (abbreviation for Oosterdokseiland) is a fixed bridge in the center of the Dutch capital Amsterdam that connects Oosterdokseiland with Prins Hendrikkade. The bridge consists of prefabricated concrete elements, steel and aluminum and consists of three parts.

name: Oetewalerbrug
en: The Oetewalerbrug (bridge no. 189) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. It spans the Ringvaart of the Watergraafsmeer, connecting the Linnaeusstraat, called Oetewalerweg until 1878, with the Middenweg in the former Overamstelse Polder and the reclaimed Watergraafsmeer. Until 1896 it lay on a municipal boundary.

name: Oetewalerbrug
en: The Oetewalerbrug (bridge no. 189) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. It spans the Ringvaart of the Amsterdam Watergraafsmeer. It provides the connection between Linnaeusstraat, until 1878 Oetewalerweg, and Middenweg in the former Overamstelse Polder with the Watergraafsmeer drainage works.

name: Olympiahuis
en: The Olympic House (the house on Stadionplein nr. 18), also known as the Gatekeeper's House, or Northern Service House, is a former gatekeeper's house on the grounds in Amsterdam, where the 1928 Olympic Games took place. During these games, it served as a post office. Like the Olympic Stadium, it was designed by architect Jan Wils. The O

name: Olympiahuis
en: The Olympiahuisje, the small building at Stadionplein 18, also called the Portiershuisje or Noordelijke Dienstwoning, is a former porter's house on the Amsterdam grounds where the 1928 Olympic Games were held. During those games it served as a post office. Like the Olympic Stadium it was designed by the architect Jan Wils.

name: Omvalbrug
en: The Omvalbrug, bridge no. 429, is a lift bridge between the Amsterdam districts of Watergraafsmeer and Overamstel. It lies close to the Amstelstation, in the Spaklerweg, and crosses the Weespertrekvaart beside the elevated rail and metro line. It dates from 1953 but only came into use for traffic once the Spaklerweg opened.

name: Omvalbrug
en: The Omvalbrug, bridge no. 429, is a movable bridge between the Amsterdam neighborhoods of Watergraafsmeer and Overamstel. The bridge is located near Amstel station and is located in Spaklerweg and crosses the Weespertrekvaart next to the elevated railway and metro track.

name: Onze Lieve Vrouwe Kapel
en: The Onze Lieve Vrouwe Kapel is a chapel in Amsterdam-Oost. It is located on the south side of the Ruyschstraat/ 's-Gravesandeplein in Amsterdam.

name: Oost-Indische Huisbrug
en: The Oost-Indische Huisbrug (bridge 223) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge spans the Kloveniersburgwal and thus forms the connection between Russia and the southern quay of the Raamgracht. The bridge has been a municipal monument since October 10, 1995.

name: Oost-Indische Huisbrug
en: The Oost-Indische Huisbrug (bridge 223) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Kloveniersburgwal, connecting the Rusland with the southern quay of the Raamgracht. It has been a municipal monument since 10 October 1995 and is named after the Oost-Indisch Huis on the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal and the Oude Hoogstraat.

name: Oosterbeerbrug
en: The Oosterbeerbrug (bridge 354) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Oosterparkkerk
en: The Oosterparkkerk stands on the west side of the Oosterpark in Amsterdam, in the Oosterparkbuurt.

name: Opstandingskerk
en: The Opstandingskerk is a church in Amsterdam West, at Bos en Lommerplein 325 on the western part of the square. While it was still being built it acquired the nickname Kolenkit, coal scuttle, because its 48-metre bell tower resembles one. The name stuck so well that the surrounding neighbourhood was named after it: the Kolenkitbuurt.

name: Orgelpark
en: The Orgelpark is an arts centre in Amsterdam devoted to the organ, opened on 20 January 2007. It makes it possible to combine organ music with other art forms such as dance, ballet and theatre. There are several organs as well as other keyboard instruments.

name: Orgelpark
en: The Orgelpark is an art center in Amsterdam where the organ is central. It was opened on January 20, 2007. The Orgelpark provides the opportunity to combine organ music with other forms of art, such as dance, ballet and theater. There are several organs, but also other keyboard instruments present.

name: Osdorperwegbrug
en: The Osdorperwegbrug, also known as Viaduct Rijksweg 5 – Osdorperweg and designated Kunstwerk 512 by Rijkswaterstaat, is a viaduct over the Osdorperweg in Amsterdam. It lies in the Westrandweg, the part of the A5 motorway that also crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. It was designed by Zwarts & Jansma Architecten.

name: Osdorperwegbrug
en: The Osdorperwegbrug, also known as Viaduct Rijksweg 5 - Osdorperweg, designated by the Rijkswaterstaat operator as Work of Art 512, is a viaduct over the Osdorperweg in the municipality of Amsterdam. The building is located on the Westrandweg, a part of the A5 motorway that also runs over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer.

name: Oude Haagsebrug
en: The Oude Haagsebrug (bridge no. 1864) was a bridge over the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer on the route between Amsterdam, via the hamlet of Nieuwe Meer, and Schiphol. The road over this bridge is the Oude Haagseweg, the former Rijksweg 4.

name: Oude Kinkerbrug
en: The Oude Kinkerbrug (bridge 169) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It connects the Elandsgracht with the Kinkerstraat, spanning the Singelgracht between them. The Appeltjesmarkt lies to its north-east and Amsterdam's police headquarters of 1941 to its south-east. The Europarking car park is also nearby.

name: Oude Lutherse Kerk
en: The Oude Lutherse Kerk at Singel 411, corner Spui, in Amsterdam is a Lutheran church, built on the site where the Lutheran congregation hall used to stand. The church was built between 1632 and 1633 under the direction of Wessel Becker and Willem van Daelen.

name: Oudemanhuispoort
en: Oudemanhuispoort, often abbreviated to OMHP, is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam between the Spui and the Waterlooplein. It is one of the main sites of the University of Amsterdam and houses the faculty of humanities. Built in the 17th century around a courtyard, it was originally a hospice for old men and women, and is a protected monument.

name: Oudemanhuispoort
en: Oudemanhuispoort (often abbreviated as: OMHP) is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam, between the Spui and the Waterlooplein. It is one of the main locations of the University of Amsterdam, the faculty of humanities is located there. name: Overschiebrug-Noord
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two works of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat. They provide the connection between the Henk Sneevlietweg and the Rijksweg 10/Ringweg-West.

name: Overschiebrug-Zuid
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two works of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat. They provide the connection between the Henk Sneevlietweg and the Rijksweg 10/Ringweg-West.

name: Overschiebrug-Zuid
en: The Overschiebrug-Noord (bridge 655) and Overschiebrug-Zuid (bridge 665) are two structures in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The two viaducts span the Overschiestraat and link the Henk Sneevlietweg with Rijksweg 10, the western ring road. The northern bridge serves as the westbound exit and the southern one as the on-ramp from the west.

name: P.W. Janssen
en: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a memorial on the Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West. The sculpture by Bart van Hove was unveiled on 29 May 1908 by Jacob Theodoor Cremer, former minister of colonies and chairman of the committee, who wanted a memorial to Peter Wilhelm Janssen, entrepreneur, philanthropist and co-founder of the Deli Maatschappij.

name: P.W. Janssen
en: The Monument Peter Wilhelm Janssen is a monument on Bellamyplein in Amsterdam-West. name: Paleis voor Volksvlijtbrug
en: The Paleis voor Volksvlijtbrug (bridge no. 248) is a fixed bridge on the boundary of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-Zuid. It connects the Westeinde on the north side with the Stadhouderskade, the south quay of the Singelgracht, and the Van Woustraat, spanning the Singelgracht. Tram line 4 runs over it.

name: Pancratiuskerk
en: The Sint-Pancratiuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in the village of Sloten. The first Sloten church is first mentioned in a charter of Bishop Willem I of Gelre from 1063. It may have stood near the present Van Suchtelen van de Haarestraat in Osdorp, between the Osdorpplein and Hoekenes. The village has been on its present site since about 1175.

name: Pancratiuskerk
en: The Sint-Pancratiuskerk is a Roman Catholic church in the village of Sloten. The first Sloterkerk is first mentioned in a charter of Bishop Willem I (van Gelre) from 1063. name: Pastoorsbrug
en: The Pastoorsbrug (bridge 55) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the southern quay of the Brouwersgracht and crosses the Keizersgracht, making it the northernmost bridge over that canal, which does not continue beyond the Brouwersgracht. Too young to be a monument itself, it is surrounded by national monuments.

name: Pastoorsbrug
en: The Pastoorsbrug (bridge 55) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the southern quay of the Brouwersgracht and crosses the Keizersgracht. It is therefore the northernmost bridge over that canal that does not continue on the other side of the Brouwersgracht.

name: Pathé City
en: The Pathé City is a Pathé cinema at Kleine-Gartmanplantsoen 15-19 in Amsterdam, 40 meters from Leidseplein and diagonally opposite De Balie. The cinema is located in the City Theater building, a theater building from 1935. Initially, it was set up with a single large theater hall. name: Pathé de Munt
en: Pathé de Munt is a large cinema in the center of Amsterdam of cinema operator Pathé. The cinema is located on Vijzelstraat not far from another Pathé cinema: Pathé Tuschinski in Reguliersbreestraat. Both cinemas border each other behind the shops on Reguliersbreestraat. name: Pelikaanbrug
en: The Pelikaanbrug (bridge number 277) is a lifting bridge from 1984 in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Oosterkerk. The bridge spans the Nieuwe Vaart, from the Hoogte Kadijk in the south to the Wittenburgergracht in the north. The bridge is exclusively accessible to pedestrians and cyclists. The bridge is named after the pelican, but also after the nearby former

name: Pelikaanbrug
en: The Pelikaanbrug (bridge number 277) is a drawbridge from 1984 in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Oosterkerk. It spans the Nieuwe Vaart from the Hoogte Kadijk in the south to the Wittenburgergracht in the north, and is open only to pedestrians and cyclists. It is named after the pelican, and also after a nearby former works of that name.

name: Peter Postbrug
en: The Peter Postbrug (bridge 2162) is a structure in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The Laan van Spartaan district in which it lies was laid out in the 2000s. Sports fields once on the city's edge became surrounded by building as Amsterdam needed room for housing, and a new district with new drainage channels was created.

name: Peter Postbrug
en: The Peter Postbrug (bridge 2162) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The district Laan van Spartaan, in which this bridge is located, was developed in the early 21st century. name: Petruskerk
en: The Petruskerk is a Protestant church in the former village of Sloterdijk, now part of Amsterdam-West.

name: Pia Beckbrug
en: The Pia Beckbrug (bridge number 1868) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Slotervaart in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The bridge was built to open up a neighborhood, whose names are named after jazz musicians such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie.

name: Pia Beckbrug
en: The Pia Beckbrug (bridge number 1868) is a fixed bridge in Slotervaart, Amsterdam Nieuw-West. It was built to open up a district whose streets are named after jazz musicians such as Louis Armstrong, Duke Ellington and Count Basie. It was built in the late 1980s and early 1990s and lies in the Louis Armstrongstraat.

name: Pianola Museum
en: The Pianola Museum in the Jordaan is a music museum in Amsterdam that offers an overview of the history and way of playing the pianola, a 'self-playing' musical instrument that was built between 1900 and around 1935. The museum's collection includes more than 100 instruments from that time. Regular concerts with kl take place in the museum

name: Piet Bakkerbrug
en: The Piet Bakkerbrug (bridge number 715) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The traffic bridge, which also carries bus line 63, lies in the Pieter Calandlaan and spans the Christoffel Plantijngracht. It has seven lanes: footway, cycle path and carriageway eastbound, a central island, then carriageway and cycle path westbound.

name: Piet Bakkerbrug
en: The Piet Bakkerbrug (bridge number 715) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam Nieuw-West. The traffic bridge, over which bus line 63 also runs, is located in Pieter Calandlaan and spans the Christoffel Plantijngracht.

name: Piet Keizerbrug
en: The Piet Keizerbrug (bridge 2234) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is a pedestrian and bicycle bridge; it forms the connection between the Esplanade de Meer square and the Stade de Colombes (street). It lies parallel to the Sjaak Swartbrug over a decorative water.

name: Piet Keizerbrug
en: The Piet Keizerbrug (bridge 2234) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is a foot and cycle bridge connecting the Esplanade de Meer square with the Stade de Colombes. It runs parallel to the Sjaak Swartbrug over an ornamental water in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002.

name: Piet Meerburgbrug
en: The Piet Meerburgbrug (bridge 234) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge spans two parallel diving boards. These diving boards connect a ornamental pond in the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam with the water of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.

name: Piet Meerburgbrug
en: The Piet Meerburgbrug (bridge 234) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The traffic bridge crosses two parallel culverts, which connect an ornamental pond in the Hortus Botanicus Amsterdam with the water of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht. It links the Hortusplantsoen on the west side with the northern quay of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht.

name: Pieter Goemansbrug
en: The Pieter Goemansbrug is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is named after the lyricist Pieter Goemans and was previously known unofficially as the Bestedelingenbrug or Bestedelingensluis, after the nearby Bestedelingenhuis, a refuge for orphans and the poor, which was merged with the then Palace of Justice in 1950.

name: Pieter Goemansbrug
en: The Pieter Goemansbrug is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is named after writer Pieter Goemans and was previously officially known as Bestedelingenbrug and/or Bestedelingensluis after the once nearby Bestedelingenhuis (care for orphans and poverty spreaders or, in other words, settlements), which was merged in 1950 with the then-Palace of

name: Planciusspoorbrug
en: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum in the Netherlands. The bridge spans the north-south running Planciusstraat, its direct namesake, both are named after Petrus Plancius. Until November 2017, the bridge was known as S6 and S7 (rail bridge 6 and 7).

name: Planciusspoorbrug
en: The Planciusspoorbrug is a railway viaduct in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the north-south Planciusstraat, from which it takes its name; both are named after Petrus Plancius. Until November 2017 the bridge was known as S6 and S7, when the city renamed all the railway bridges in Amsterdam.

name: Plaquette Chet Baker
en: The Chet Baker plaque is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Centrum, a small tribute to the trumpeter Chet Baker. On the night of 12-13 May 1988 he fell from the window of Hotel Prins Hendrik at Prins Hendrikkade 52-58, probably under the influence, and was left almost unrecognisable by his fall onto a bollard.

name: Plaquette Chet Baker
en: The Plaquette Chet Baker is an artistic work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum. It is a small tribute to the trumpeter Chet Baker. He died on the night of May 12 to 13, 1988, presumably under the influence, falling out of the window of Hotel Prins Hendrik, located at Prins Hendrikkade 52-58. He was almost unrecognizable after falling on a canal boat in Amsterdam.

name: Plein Theater
en: The PleinTheater in Amsterdam-Oost is a stage for small-scale theatre, dance, contemporary classical music, youth theatre and neighbourhood activities.

name: Posthoornkerk
en: The Posthoornkerk, official name Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, is a church building on Haarlemmerstraat in Amsterdam. The architect of the Posthoornkerk was P.J.H. Cuypers, who designed the building in 1860. The church replaced the dilapidated hiding church De Posthoorn on the Prinsengracht, whose name was taken over, after an earlier attempt by

name: Postjesbrug
en: Brug 231 may refer to Brug 231 (Houtgracht), a bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum over the Houtgracht, which was filled in in 1882, or Brug 231 (Postjeswetering), a bridge in Amsterdam-West from 1919/1920.

name: Praterlaan
en: The Gerrie Mührenbrug (bridge 2235) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the traffic bridges — the others are for slow traffic — within the Park de Meer neighbourhood in the Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002. That neighbourhood is entirely surrounded by a ring ditch.

name: Raampoort
en: Raampoort may refer to the Raampoort in Amsterdam, in Deventer, or in Haarlem.

name: Radioweg
en: The Velibor Vasović Bridge (bridge 1906) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. A concrete bridge, but then under number 426, provided the connection between the Watergraafsmeer district and the neighboring municipality of Diemen from 1983. These were then separated by the Ringweg-Oost and a ring ditch of Diemen. A joint span was then chosen.

name: Radioweg
en: The Velibor Vasovićbrug (bridge 1906) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. From 1983 a concrete bridge, then numbered 426, connected the Watergraafsmeer district with the neighbouring municipality of Diemen, which were separated by the eastern ring road and a Diemen ring ditch. A single shared span was chosen at the time.

name: Ravensbrück memorial
en: Vrouwen van Ravensbrück 1940-1945 is a monument on the Museumplein in Amsterdam commemorating the Dutch victims of Ravensbrück, the Nazi concentration camp for women in Germany.

name: Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge
en: The Raw Aron Schuster Synagoge or the Obrechtsjoel (בית כנסת רב אהרן שוסטר) is the largest still functioning Ashkenazi synagogue (shoe) in Amsterdam. The synagogue, located at the corner of Jacob Obrechtplein and Heinzestraat in Amsterdam-Zuid, is part of the Jewish Community in Amsterdam, the NIHS. Most choepot (Jewish weddings) are held here.

name: Reesluis
en: The Reesluis (bridge 64) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Rembrandt van Rijn statue
en: The Rembrandt monument is a 19th-century memorial to the painter Rembrandt van Rijn on the Rembrandtplein in Amsterdam. It is the oldest surviving statue in Amsterdam and was the first statue of a visual artist in the Netherlands.

name: Riekerhavenbrug
en: Bridge 307 is a metal lifting bridge in southwest Amsterdam. The pedestrian and cyclist bridge is located in the Jaagpad and spans the halfway line between the Riekerhaven and Schinkel. Less than 10 meters west lies the Uiverbrug (bridge 2208), a "real" traffic bridge that has been connecting the Generaal Vetterstraat with the Valschermkade since 2003.

name: Riekerhavenbrug
en: Brug 307 is a metal drawbridge in the south-west of Amsterdam. The foot and cycle bridge lies in the Jaagpad and spans the dividing line between the Riekerhaven and the Schinkel. Less than 10 metres to the west lies the Uiverbrug (bridge 2208), a proper traffic bridge that has connected the Generaal Vetterstraat with the Valschermkade since 2003.

name: Rijksakademie van beeldende kunsten
en: The Royal Academy of Fine Arts (also Royal Academy of Fine Arts) in Amsterdam was the highest art training institution in the Kingdom of the Netherlands from 1820 to 1870. Until 1830, it shared this role with the academy of Antwerp. The Academy was the successor to the City Drawing Academy. In 1870, the Academy was abolished and replaced by the

name: Ringvaartbrug A5
en: The Ringvaartbrug A5, designated as Work of Art 511, is a work of art in the province of North Holland. The structure is located on the Rijksweg 5 / Westrandweg and crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. The architectural firm Zwarts & Jansma Architecten was responsible for the design of this national road and all its works of art.

name: Ringvaartbrug A5
en: The Ringvaartbrug A5, designated Kunstwerk 511, is a structure in the province of North Holland. It lies in Rijksweg 5, the Westrandweg, and crosses the Ringvaart of the Haarlemmermeer. Zwarts & Jansma Architecten were responsible for the design of this motorway and all its structures.

name: Rosa Overbeekbrug
en: The Rosa Overbeekbrug (bridge no. 121) is a bridge over the Bloemgracht in the Jordaan in Amsterdam, connecting the Eerste Bloemdwarsstraat with the Tweede Leliedwarsstraat. A bridge has been here for centuries: both Balthasar Florisz. van Berckenrode and Joan Blaeu drew one on their maps of 1625 and 1649.

name: Rotterdammerbrug
en: The Rotterdammerbrug (bridge 150) is a fixed bridge on the boundary of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-West. It spans the Singelgracht between the Marnixstraat and the Nassaukade. On the east side it meets the Eerste Marnixplantsoen, laid out on the former Bolwerk Haarlem, one of Amsterdam's 17th-century bastions.

name: Rotterdammerbrug
en: The Rotterdammerbrug (bridge 150) is a fixed bridge on the border of Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam Oud-West. The bridge spans the Singelgracht between Marnixstraat and Nassaukade. On the east side, the bridge opens into Eerste Marnixplantsoen, built on the former Bolwerk Haarlem, one of the 17th-century Amsterdam bastions. The first bridge was a bo

name: Royal Tropical Institute
en: The KIT building is a complex of buildings in Amsterdam-Oost, built from 1915 to 1926 for the accommodation of the Colonial Institute and museum. The architect Johannes van Nieukerken designed the building. After his death in 1913, it was then completed by his sons Johan and Marie Adrianus van Nieukerken. It was financed by contributions from among others

name: Rozenoordmetrobrug
en: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam. The bridges connect Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two traffic bridges are three railway bridges; one for the Amsterdam metro and two for the train traffic of the Dutch Railways on the Weesp - Leiden railway line. All b

name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
en: The Rozenoordbrug (bridge no. 174P, A10) consists of two traffic bridges over the river Amstel in Amsterdam, connecting Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two road bridges lie three railway bridges: one for the Amsterdam metro and two for Nederlandse Spoorwegen trains on the Weesp-Leiden line.

name: Rozenoordspoorbrug
en: The Rozenoord Bridge (bridge no. 174P (A10)) consists of two traffic bridges over the Amstel River in Amsterdam. The bridges connect Amsterdam-Zuid with Overamstel. Between the two traffic bridges are three railway bridges; one for the Amsterdam metro and two for the train traffic of the Dutch Railways on the Weesp - Leiden railway line. All b

name: Ruud Krolbrug
en: The Ruud Krolbrug (bridge 2232) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost. It is one of the foot and cycle bridges in the Park de Meer neighbourhood in Watergraafsmeer, built here between 1998 and 2002 and entirely surrounded by a ring ditch. It connects the Wembleylaan, inside the neighbourhood, with the Radioweg outside it.

name: Ruud Krolbrug
en: The Ruud Krolbrug (bridge 2232) is a structural work of art in Amsterdam-Oost. The bridge is one of the pedestrian and bicycle bridges in the area of Park de Meer, Watergraafsmeer that rose from the ground here between 1998 and 2002. That area is completely surrounded by a water channel/ring ditch.

name: Ryckerbrug
en: The Rijckerbrug or Ryckerbrug (bridge no. 167) is a fixed slab bridge between Amsterdam-Centrum and Amsterdam-West crossing the Singelgracht. It connects the Rozengracht, called the Verlengde Rozengracht while it was being built, with the De Clercqstraat, and has its western abutment in the Nassaukade.

name: Samen Spelen Samen Leven
en: The Kindermonument Markt voor Joden, also called Samen spelen, samen leven, is an artistic work in Amsterdam-Zuid. It is a group of three sculptures by Truus Menger-Oversteegen, placed since 1986 at the entrance to the playground on the Gaaspstraat, between the even-numbered buildings on the Vechtstraat and the odd-numbered ones on the Gaaspstraat.

name: Sarphatimonument
en: The Sarphatimonument honours the 19th-century Jewish Amsterdam physician and benefactor Samuel Sarphati and stands in the Sarphatipark in the De Pijp district. It was built in 1886 on a small mound made for it in the park. It is a round, temple-like stone structure 12 metres high, designed by Jacobus Roeland de Kruijff.

name: Sarphatimonument
en: The Sarphatimonument is a monument in honor of the 19th-century Jewish Amsterdam physician and benefactor Samuel Sarphati, in Sarphatipark in the Amsterdam district of de Pijp. The monument was built in 1886 on a small hill specially built for this purpose in the park.

name: Schellingwouderbrug
en: The Schellingwouderbrug (bridge no. 55P) is a traffic bridge over the Buiten IJ in Amsterdam, connecting Zeeburgereiland in Amsterdam-Oost with Amsterdam-Noord. In line with it lies the Amsterdamsebrug over the Amsterdam-Rijnkanaal, between Zeeburgereiland and the Zeeburgerdijk near the Flevopark in the Indische Buurt.

name: Schellingwouderbrug
en: The Schellingwouderbrug (bridge no. 55P) is a traffic bridge over the Buiten IJ in Amsterdam. The bridge connects the Zeeburgereiland (Amsterdam-East) and Amsterdam-North with each other.

name: Schollenbrug
en: The Schollenbrug (bridge 340) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Oost. The traffic bridge lies in the Weesperzijde and spans the Ringvaart of the Watergraafsmeer at the Amstel.

name: Shadow quay
en: De Schaduwkade is a monument to two hundred Jewish residents of the Nieuwe Keizersgracht in Amsterdam who were murdered in the Second World War. It consists of two hundred metal plates bearing the residents' names, grouped around the number of the house where they lived on the other side of the water.

name: Simon Carmiggelt
en: The Bust of Simon Carmiggelt is a work of art in Amsterdam-Centrum. In November 1987, writer Simon Carmiggelt, a well-known Amsterdam personality, died. Soon after, the idea came up to have a statue erected in the city as a tribute. Friends, acquaintances of the writer and the public under the leadership of actor Ton van Duinhoven raised money. name: Singelgrachtbrug
en: The Houtmanspoorbrug, colloquially known as the Singelgrachtbrug, is a system of lift bridges in Amsterdam-Centrum, near the Spaarndammerbuurt district. The bridge spans the Westerkanaal with its western quay, the Houtmankade. Until November 2017, the bridge was known as S4 (rail bridge 4) or Singelgrachtbrug. The Westerkanaal is indeed part of the Singelgra

name: Singelgrachtbrug
en: The Houtmanspoorbrug, popularly called the Singelgrachtbrug, is a set of drawbridges in Amsterdam-Centrum on the edge of the Spaarndammerbuurt. It spans the Westerkanaal and its western quay, the Houtmankade. Until November 2017 it was known as S4 or the Singelgrachtbrug, as the Westerkanaal lies in line with the Singelgracht.

name: Singelkerk
en: The Singelkerk is a church of the Mennonite congregation in Amsterdam, lying between the Singel and the Herengracht. It is a clandestine church, one that is not recognisable as a church from the outside.

name: Sint Nicolaasbrug
en: The Sint Nicolaasbrug (bridge 306) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge spans the Open Havenfront and extends along the Damrak. The bridge connects the Prins Hendrikkade with the Stationsplein in front of Amsterdam Central Station. This led to its unofficial name Stationsbrug. Since it was the middle of three bridges in front of the s

name: Sint Nicolaasbrug
en: The Sint Nicolaasbrug (bridge 306) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Open Havenfront in line with the Damrak, connecting the Prins Hendrikkade with the Stationsplein in front of Amsterdam Centraal station. That gave it the unofficial name Stationsbrug, as it was the middle of the three bridges to the station.

name: Sint Olofskapel
en: The Sint-Olofkapel, or Oudezijds Kapel, is a building in the Dutch city of Amsterdam. The former church building is located in the city center of Amsterdam, between the Zeedijk and the Nieuwebrugsteeg, near the Damrak. The first Sint Olofskapel was built between 1440 and 1450 against a large city gate, the Sint Olofspoort.

name: Sint Olofskapel
en: The Sint-Olofskapel, or Oudezijds Kapel, is a building in Amsterdam. The former church stands in the inner city between the Zeedijk and the Nieuwebrugsteeg, near the Damrak. The first Sint-Olofskapel was built between 1440 and 1450 against a large city gate, the Sint Olofspoort, which was demolished in 1618.

name: Sint-Agneskerk
en: The Sint-Agneskerk in Amsterdam is a Catholic parish church, located at the corner of Amstelveenseweg 163 and Cornelis Krusemanstraat, on the Haarlemmermeercircuit and on the edge of the Willemspark neighborhood.

name: Sint-Agneskerk
en: The Sint-Agneskerk in Amsterdam is a Catholic parish church on the corner of Amstelveenseweg 163 and the Cornelis Krusemanstraat, at the Haarlemmermeercircuit on the edge of the Willemsparkbuurt. Dedicated to the martyr St Agnes, it was built between 1919 and 1932 to a design by the architect Jan Stuyt and listed as a national monument in 1996.

name: Sint-Gertrudiskerk
en: The Sint-Gertrudiskerk is a former Roman Catholic church building in the village of Ruigoord in the municipality of Amsterdam in the Dutch province of North Holland. The church was designed by C.P.W. Dessing and was dedicated to the Holy Gertrude of Nijvel. In the church there is a statue of Gertrudis with a staff with mice.

name: Sint-Gertrudiskerk
en: The Sint-Gertrudiskerk is a former Roman Catholic church in the village of Ruigoord in the municipality of Amsterdam, North Holland. It was designed by C.P.W. Dessing and dedicated to St Gertrude of Nivelles. Inside stands a statue of Gertrude with a staff and mice. The church was taken out of use in 1973.

name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk
en: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is an Old Catholic church on the Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam. The church, presbytery and teaching room form a whole and were designed by Johan W.F. Hartkamp jr., a pupil of Hendrik Petrus Berlage. The complex was completed in 1914 as a continuation of the clandestine church De Ooievaar.

name: Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk
en: The Sint-Petrus-en-Pauluskerk is a Dutch Old Catholic church building on Ruysdaelstraat in the Duivelseiland district of Amsterdam. The church, parsonage and teaching room form a whole and were designed by Johan W.F. Hartkamp jr., a pupil of Hendrik Petrus Berlage. The church complex was completed in 1914 as a precursor to the secret church 'De Ooievaar'

name: Sloterbrug
en: The Sloterbrug (bridge 9P) is a drawbridge within the municipality of Haarlemmermeer. The bridge belongs to Haarlemmermeer but is known in Amsterdam as bridge 9P, the P meaning not maintained by Amsterdam. Officially the bridge has no name.

name: Sloterdijkerbrug
en: The Sloterdijkerbrug (bridge 321) is a double wooden drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Prinseneilandsgracht. It not only forms the main route between Sloterdijkstraat on the mainland and Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland, but also between both quays of that canal Nieuwe Teertuinen and Prinseneiland, the street. Around the bridge is a

name: Sloterdijkerbrug
en: The Sloterdijkerbrug (bridge 321) is a double wooden drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Prinseneilandsgracht, forming both the through route between the Sloterdijkstraat on the mainland and the Galgenstraat on Prinseneiland, and the link between that canal's two quays, the Nieuwe Teertuinen and Prinseneiland.

name: Sloterkerk
en: The Sloterkerk is a Protestant church in Sloten, North Holland.

name: Solitudobrug
en: The Solitudobrug (bridge 2190) is a structure in Amsterdam-Oost.

name: Solitudolaanspoorbrug
en: The Solitudolaanspoorbrug lies in Amsterdam-Oost, along with the Solitudolaan and the Solitudopad. The lane and path were named in 2015, when new housing was built in the area and the roads were rearranged; the railway bridge was named after the lane in February 2018. The viaduct was built in two stages.

name: Solitudolaanspoorbrug
en: The Solitudolaanspoorbrug, whose coordinates are Solitudolaan and Solitudopad in Amsterdam-Oost. The Solitudolaan and -pad received their names in 2015, when new residential buildings were built in this area and road redevelopment took place. The railway bridge was named after the avenue in February 2018.

name: Spanjemonument
en: The Spanjemonument is an artistic work and war memorial in Amsterdam-Noord.

name: Staalmeestersbrug
en: The Staalmeestersbrug (bridge 227) is a drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Groenburgwal and lies in the Staalstraat, which runs along both sides of that canal. With bridge 226 it is one of only two bridges over the canal. A municipal monument since 1995, it is surrounded by municipal and national monuments.

name: Staalmeestersbrug
en: The Staalmeestersbrug (bridge 227) is a drawbridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It spans the Groenburgwal and is located in Staalstraat, which lies on both sides of the Groenburgwal. It is next to bridge 226, the only bridge over the canal.

name: Staatsliedenbrug
en: The Staatsliedenbrug (bridge 139) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West. The bridge forms the connection between the Van Limburg Stirumstraat and the Tweede Nassaustraat. It spans the Kostverlorenvaart with its quays De Wittenkade. Most of the Kostverlorenvaart is part of the Staandemast route through Amsterdam-West, but not just this section

name: Staatsliedenbrug
en: The Staatsliedenbrug (bridge 139) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam Oud-West. It connects the Van Limburg Stirumstraat with the Tweede Nassaustraat, spanning the Kostverlorenvaart and its quays at De Wittenkade. Most of the Kostverlorenvaart forms part of the Staandemastroute through Amsterdam-West, but not this stretch.

name: Steenhouwerijbrug
en: The Steenhouwerijbrug or Steenhouwerijsluis (bridge 45) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The arched bridge is located on the northeast bank of the Keizersgracht and crosses the Leidsegracht. The bridge gets its name from the Stadsmetseltuin that was located on the Leidsegracht during the planning of this neighborhood.

name: Steenhouwerijbrug
en: The Steenhouwerijbrug or Steenhouwerijsluis (bridge 45) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The arched bridge lies in the north-east bank of the Keizersgracht and crosses the Leidsegracht. It takes its name from the Stadsmetseltuin, the city masonry yard that stood on the Leidsegracht when this neighbourhood was laid out.

name: Tante Saarbrug
en: The Tante Saarbrug (bridge 31) is a fixed arch bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum.

name: Tetje de Jongbrug
en: Tetje de Jongbrug (bridge 100) is a permanent bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. The bridge is located on the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Looiersgracht. This canal has only three bridges, the Looierssluis (bridge 103), bridge 102 and this bridge 100. Bridge 101, the Nieuwe Amstelbrug, spans the Amstel, so elsewhere in the city.

name: Tetje de Jongbrug
en: Tetje de Jongbrug (bridge 100) is a fixed bridge in Amsterdam-Centrum. It lies in the eastern quay of the Lijnbaansgracht and spans the Looiersgracht. That canal has only three bridges: the Looierssluis (bridge 103), bridge 102 and this one. Bridge 101, the Nieuwe Amstelbrug, crosses the Amstel elsewhere in the city.

name: The Movies
en: The Movies is a cinema in Amsterdam. The Movies is the oldest still in use cinema in Amsterdam. The complex is located at Haarlemmerdijk 161-163 on the outskirts of the Jordaan.
